title: Retain buffered hosted Partition and Uniform direct output for guarded follow-up
question: Can hosted plain Partition followed by Uniform avoid an encoded snapshot and improve complete Run while preserving its resource and publication contracts?
summary: The 512 KiB writer saves 0.30–0.40 s in all nine matched external pairs and about 105 MB each of temporary reads and writes. Both buffered arms complete under a 190 MiB temporary cap that denies snapshot Run. Preserve hosted Auto memory sizing with direct output.

workloads: Hosted plain Partition followed by explicit Uniform, eight repeating keys, one worker, 32 or 128 MiB, synthetic resident and 105 MB external fixtures.
Automatic memory on the same 420,003-row input with no Analyze hint. The matched route retains the 1,024 MiB sizing tier and resident sort.
Separate 190 MiB managed temporary quota at a fixed 32 MiB working budget.

validation.summary: Verified every row and field, group lineage, file naming and caps, observed route, marker readback, workspace retirement and 21 fault controls. The managed-quota control records the baseline denial and two complete direct exports.

limitations: One WSL2 host with bundled Chromium and test-provided OPFS handles.
The 64 KiB writer regresses and route-only automatic sizing adds spills.
Combined logical storage remains near the snapshot peak in spilling cells. Matching fixed-budget reservation peaks and successful admission do not characterize shared or near-limit overlap.
exclusions: Native timing, actual desktop picker destinations, device I/O and RSS, high fanout, compressed output, other pipeline shapes and arbitrary Auto workloads.
reopen_when: Reproduce the result with a real desktop destination and a matched late-admission control through the first final writer, including a held-out workload and the existing Auto tier.
